newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Cash-rich Kuwaiti firm to move funds to Far East.
newsitem.headline: Cash-rich Kuwaiti firm to move funds to Far East.

text.p: The Kuwait-based National Industries Co NIC, which has over $300 million invested abroad, said on Tuesday it plans to gradually move its investment portfolio to emerging markets from the West.

"We are intending to move from the West to emerging economies as a general trend," NIC's Chief General Manager Robert Kottritsch said. "We feel that over the next period the emerging economies are going to become a more stable bet."
NIC's cash reserves are mainly run by four international fund managers which are investing in Western markets.
But they would "probably suffer a little bit in the next few years...We are probably looking at the Far East rather than Latin America," he told Reuters in an interview.
The company, which last year paid $154 million for the aquisition of the Birmingham-based BI Group PLC, on Tuesday reported a 27 percent rise in 1996 net profit to $84 million.
"We have now several operating divisions. We have BI Group PLC, our building materials business, our steel businesses is another, and we have several more in prospect...
"Outside of that we have a lot of cash...Business has been profitable for many years and built up reserves," he added.

The company, one of the Arab world's largest listed firms, is aiming to increase its industrial assets to $1 billion by 2005 from over $300 million, raising the share of return from industrial projects to 75 percent of total income.

"If you look at a year ago, over three-quaters of our income is coming from our financial investments. We do not intend to reduce the size but what we are doing is leveraging...so that eventually...three-quarters of income comes from operations."
